Home / Finance / News / Individuals exempt from reporting foreign earnings; RBI to issue FAQs soon

Individuals exempt from reporting foreign earnings; RBI to issue FAQs soon Even in the case of entities, there is a provision for self-declaration up to a cap of ₹10 lakh per bill, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said

Reserve Bank of India | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 07 2026 | 6:23 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Clarifying that individuals do not need to report imports or export earnings, the Reserve Bank on Wednesday said it will publish FAQs (frequently asked questions) shortly to quell "misunderstandings" around the recently implemented regulatory changes. Even in the case of entities, there is a provision for self-declaration up to a cap of ₹10 lakh per bill, Governor Sanjay Malhotra said. Malhotra said the unified Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, implemented from October 1, get services players on par with merchandise entities when it comes to reporting requirements. "...individuals are not included with respect to the reporting requirements for contracts of a personal nature. There seems to be some misunderstanding on the reporting obligations. We will clarify through an FAQ shortly," Deputy Governor Rohit Jain said.

He said the new regulations are aimed at simplification and promoting ease of doing business, and added that sufficient time was given to the members of trade as the guidelines were published in January this year. Malhotra also said that the reporting on the RBI platform is to be done by intermediaries, including banks or authorised dealers and not by the exporters or importers. "...we feel it is not a major inconvenience or a burden," he said, adding that some of the information was already being shared by the importers and exporters with the intermediaries.

item.title: RBI changes stance to 'calibrated tightening': Here's what it means
item.description: The RBI's new calibrated tightening stance signals that further rate hikes remain possible as the central bank responds to inflation and economic risks ...
item.dc:creator: Sarjna Rai
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Wednesday shifted gears on monetary policy, moving from a ‘neutral’ stance to ‘calibrated tightening’ in its October 2026 Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) review. The change comes alongside a 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate to 5.5 per cent, marking the first rate hike since February 2023. What is calibrated tightening? A ‘calibrated tightening’ stance means the RBI is leaning towards tighter monetary policy, with rate cuts not being considered in the current policy cycle. If further rate hikes are needed, they are likely to be gradual and measured rather than aggressive. The RBI will assess inflation, growth, and other economic conditions before deciding whether to raise rates further. Any increase is expected to be gradual and measured, and the central bank can also adjust rates between scheduled MPC meetings if necessary. ALSO READ: RBI MPC hikes repo rate by 25 bps to 5.25%: A look at last five hikesWhy has the RBI shifted its stance? The change comes as inflation risks have increased and global conditions have become less favourable. Retail inflation rose to 4.82 per cent in August, moving above the RBI’s 4 per cent target for the third consecutive month. Higher crude oil prices and pressure on the rupee have added to concerns about imported inflation.

item.title: RBI MPC raises FY27 inflation forecast to 5.2%, projects GDP growth at 7.1%
item.description: At its policy meeting, held between October 5 and October 7, the committee changed the stance to 'caliberated tightening' ...
item.dc:creator: Vrinda Goel
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), in its October monetary policy review, raised the FY27 consumer price index (CPI)-based inflation forecast to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent, while raising the real gross domestic product (GDP) growth projection to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent. “In light of the available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year,” RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said. The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) on Wednesday unanimously hiked the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5 per cent from 5.25 per cent and changed the stance to ‘calibrated tightening’. The RBI changed the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate to 5.25 per cent, while the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate and the bank rate were changed to 5.75 per cent. Inflation forecast raised The RBI raised its FY27 CPI inflation forecast to 5.2 per cent from 5 per cent in the October monetary policy review, announced RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra. The quarterly inflation projections are: Q2 FY27: 4.9 per centQ3 FY27: 6 per centQ4 FY27: 5.7 per centQ1 FY28: 5.6 per cent Explaining the forecast, the RBI governor said CPI-based inflation increased to 4.8 per cent in August 2026 from 4.5 per cent in July. While the increase has been predominantly on account of higher inflation in the food and fuel groups, core inflation has also picked up, indicating some signs of widening price pressures. Food price increases have become more broad-based, along with notable spikes in certain items such as sugar and onion. The uptick in fuel inflation in August largely reflected unfavourable base effects. Core inflation increased to 4.2 per cent, while core inflation excluding precious metals increased to 2.9 per cent in August. The weighted share of items in headline CPI recording inflation above 4 per cent increased steadily to about 37 per cent in August. The RBI governor further said that the near-term inflation outlook points towards continued supply-side pressures on account of the deficient monsoon, ongoing El Nino conditions and high energy and other commodity prices, the pass-through of which is still continuing. GDP growth forecast raised The RBI raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points to 7.1 per cent from 6.7 per cent in the August monetary policy review. The quarterly growth projections are: FY27: 7.1 per centQ2 FY27: 7.2 per centQ3 FY27: 6.9 per centQ4 FY27: 6.8 per cent Announcing the forecast hike, Malhotra said that since the last MPC meeting in August 2026, the re-escalation of the conflict in West Asia and the consequent sharp volatility in crude oil prices have kept the global economy in flux. Global growth has remained resilient. Notwithstanding these persisting global headwinds, the Indian economy has remained resilient. Strong private consumption and fixed investment, a rebound in merchandise exports and sustained buoyancy in services exports supported growth. On the supply side, the manufacturing sector grew at a robust pace. Services sector activity strengthened further, owing to buoyant domestic and external demand. Malhotra further said that, looking ahead, global economic uncertainty will continue to have some bearing on domestic economic activity. While energy prices and supply chain pressures have continued, their near-term trajectory remains uncertain amidst the lingering West Asia conflict. Their adverse impact is being contained with active diversification of supply sources. Deficient south-west monsoon and strong El Nino conditions pose risks to the agriculture sector’s outlook and rural demand, although healthy buffers of foodgrains and proactive policy interventions by the government are expected to mitigate the impact. The RBI governor said that continuing momentum in services and broadly stable employment conditions are likely to support urban demand. Strong capacity utilisation, robust credit flows and the government’s thrust on infrastructure are expected to sustain investment activity. While services exports are expected to remain buoyant, bilateral trade agreements should boost merchandise exports.

item.title: Kotak, IndusInd, Axis Bank shares jump on strong Q2 business updates
item.description: Lenders report strong credit and deposit growth aided by FCNR(B) inflows, though analysts flag concerns over CASA momentum ...
item.dc:creator: Subrata Panda
item.content:encoded: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank, IndusInd Bank and Axis Bank rose sharply on Tuesday after the lenders reported robust growth in advances and deposits in their quarterly business updates. This growth was aided by healthy mobilisation of FCNR(B) deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank’s shares jumped 3.59 per cent to close at ₹431.25 on the BSE, while IndusInd Bank gained 2.79 per cent to end at ₹906.95. Axis Bank’s shares rose 2.01 per cent to ₹1,248.50. However, RBL Bank’s shares closed 0.72 per cent lower at ₹414 on the BSE compared with the previous day’s close. On Monday, Kotak Mahindra Bank reported robust net advances (period-end) growth of 25 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) and 13 per cent quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). Excluding advances linked to FCNR(B) deposits, loan growth remained firm at around 21 per cent Y-o-Y and 10 per cent Q-o-Q. Deposits grew 23 per cent Y-o-Y and 14 per cent Q-o-Q, aided by FCNR(B) inflows. Excluding these, deposit growth was more measured at 13 per cent Y-o-Y and 4 per cent Q-o-Q. Current account savings account (CASA) balances grew 11 per cent Y-o-Y and 8 per cent Q-o-Q. The bank mobilised $5.78 billion through FCNR(B) deposits during the quarter. Axis Bank, India’s third-largest private sector lender, said its deposits grew 5.8 per cent sequentially and 20.7 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹14.52 trillion as of September 30, while gross advances rose 8.8 per cent Q-o-Q and 22.7 per cent YoY to ₹13.85 trillion. The lender mobilised $10.62 billion (₹1.02 trillion) in FCNR(B) deposits under the Reserve Bank of India’s swap facility introduced earlier this year.   “While the outcome is good on the loan growth front, the question is sustainability plus core deposit growth around 12-13 per cent for Kotak (Mahindra Bank) and Axis (Bank) isn’t that great. That goes to show that eventually loan growth will have to come down from current levels. CASA growth is also 10 to 11 per cent similar to HDFC Bank showing the pressure that exists in CASA across the system. CASA ratios continue to decline even on core deposit growth basis”, said Suresh Ganapathy, MD&Head - Financial Services Research, Macquarie Capital.  Meanwhile, IndusInd Bank’s net advances grew 11.2 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹3.62 trillion as of September 30, 2026, outpacing the 10.1 per cent growth in deposits to ₹4.29 trillion. IndusInd Bank’s CASA ratio declined to 28 per cent from 30.7 per cent a year earlier and 29.4 per cent in June. The lender mobilised $3.51 billion in FCNR(B) deposits under the RBI’s deposit swap facility, with outstanding loans of about ₹16,564 crore extended from its GIFT City branch against these deposits as of September-end. And, RBL Bank’s total deposits rose 34 per cent Y-o-Y to around ₹1.56 trillion in the quarter ended September 30 (Q2FY27), while gross advances grew 40 per cent to around ₹1.43 trillion. (Disclosure: Entities controlled by the Kotak family have a significant holding in Business Standard Pvt Ltd)
